proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10875.2 *lakkuṭa lists Prakrit lakkuḍa, Hindi lakṛī “firewood”, Gujarati lākṛũ and Marathi lākuḍ “wood”. Retained k selects the strengthened branch; Maithili lakṛī is explicitly borrowed from Hindi and is held for an immediate-donor link.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 11745 vidyullatā gives Prakrit vijjulī, Hindi bijlī/bijurī, Nepali bijuli, Gujarati vijḷī and eastern bijuḷi “lightning”. The extended l/r-bearing forms select this compound, not bare vidyut; Marathi bijlī is explicitly a Hindi loan and is held.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2389 uṣṇa gives Pali/Prakrit uṇha, Gujarati ūnũ/hunũ and Marathi ūnh/ūn “hot”. Loss of the cluster aspiration supplies the western n-bearing outcomes; the phonology is distinct from unrelated tāta and garam forms.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 5539.3 *ḍābba gives Old Gujarati ḍābaü, Gujarati ḍābũ and Kachchi ḍābo “left”. The b-bearing forms distinguish this section from *ḍāva; the deeper non-Aryan-origin hypothesis remains unresolved.
